question: At what perturbative order does time dependence first survive after the enhanced local-rest lapse constraint, and what is its leading functional form?

power_counting.B_grad_phi: O(epsilon^2) for perturbative scalar shift B=O(epsilon)

target_identities: the O(epsilon^5) dependence on the O(epsilon^3) auxiliary correction y3 is proportional to the quartic y2 Euler-Lagrange equation and therefore vanishes after y2 is eliminated
the only surviving explicit quintic time-dependent contribution is dot(phi) times the on-shell quartic spatial density/function(al), while B.grad(phi) enters no earlier than O(epsilon^6)
in composite Fourier notation, S5_time/M_Pl^2 = integral dot(phi) * [ J mu_K^2(-Delta)/(mu_K^2-Delta) J ] up to spatial integrations by parts defining the same quartic functional
there is still no quadratic kinetic operator or invertible velocity Hessian about phi=0

decision_rule.if_target_identities_hold: classify local-rest perturbation theory as nonlinear-time-degenerate: first time dependence appears linearly at quintic order on top of a vanishing quadratic propagator; require canonical/Dirac rank analysis before distinguishing nonlinear constraint removal from strong coupling
decision_rule.if_a_lower_or_quadratic_time_kernel_reap: reopen the local-rest rank-enhancement interpretation and derive that kernel explicitly

non_claims: does not by itself prove infinite strong coupling
does not compute a scattering amplitude or cutoff scale
does not establish the nonlinear number of local-rest degrees of freedom
does not include higher-spatial completion operators
does not apply to the rolling cosmological branch or strong-field/rotating backgrounds
next_gate_if_pass: perform a local canonical/Dirac rank analysis through the first nonlinear time-dependent order and in parallel quantify the minimal higher-spatial rescue coefficient allowed by the cosmological RTK kernel
